rows.sub: arm64 · Swift app over the embedded C API · Metal
rows.claim: The main platform: it builds, runs, and carries all the Miri evidence and most of the sanitizer evidence.

builds.detail: The Cargo workspace and the Xcode app build (BUILD SUCCEEDED).

hand.detail: The author ran the app directly; a menu-shortcut harness matches Ghostty on 51 actions, byte for byte.

lanes.detail: At the current reference commit: Miri (Stacked Borrows on 38 crates, Tree Borrows including the app core), ASan 10,077 tests, LSan 6,643, TSan 3,900 (two test-only fixes, then clean scoped re-runs), 6,648 workspace tests, benchmarks 14 of 14 against Ghostty. At the previous one: 404 of 404 app tests.

rows.sub: aarch64 Fedora 44 VM · Wayland and X11 · OpenGL
rows.claim: The GTK app is ported and works in a Linux VM under Wayland and X11, tested by hand and by live-window tests; never run on a real GPU or on x86_64 Linux.

builds.detail: Build and lints with the GTK, X11 and Wayland features; a release build; a Flatpak built, installed and run.

runs.detail: A live terminal in a GTK window since 07-18, rendered with software OpenGL (llvmpipe) only.

hand.detail: Tested by the author 07-18 to 07-23 on GNOME (Wayland), an Xfce X11 session and sway; later checks under nested KWin, headless mutter and the global-shortcuts portal.

lanes.detail: Workspace tests with the GTK, X11 and Wayland features and 18 of 18 live GTK window tests; Valgrind 6,746 tests at the current reference commit; at the previous one ASan 10,307, LSan 10,307, MSan 6,375, HWASan 10,183, TSan 4,536 and LSan on a live GTK window.

rows.sub: Windows 11 ARM64 VM · x86_64 MSVC under emulation, and GNU
rows.claim: It builds, lints and passes the full workspace test suite on Windows; like Ghostty at this reference commit, there is no Windows app.

builds.detail: Build and lints for MSVC, excluding libxml2, fontconfig and sentry; the C library in release; the font shaper for GNU.

runs.detail: rustty.exe builds but opens no window: at this reference commit Ghostty's only Windows runtime is the embedded library, which refuses to start on Windows.

hand.detail: A C example's output is byte-identical to the golden file; the console pseudo-terminal is driven in a unit test.

lanes.detail: A full workspace test run for x86_64 MSVC, excluding libxml2, fontconfig and sentry: 6,418 passed, 0 failed at the current reference commit (one flaky test fixed after the previous one); the font shaper's 133 tests for GNU.

rows.sub: FreeBSD 15.1 arm64 VM · GTK app, kqueue event loop
rows.claim: Built, tested and run natively on FreeBSD in an arm64 VM: the GTK app runs under X11 and Wayland, tested by hand and by live-window tests; three DMA-BUF tests need a GPU driver the VM lacks, and it was never run on amd64.

builds.detail: Built natively on FreeBSD 15.1 (arm64, in a VM) with GTK 4.20, excluding the crash reporter library, which Ghostty also builds for macOS only. Lints show no FreeBSD-specific warning; the executable is not position-independent, as Ghostty's default (10-11).

runs.detail: The app reports its GTK runtime, OpenGL renderer and kqueue event loop. A GTK window with a live shell ran under X11 and Wayland: typing, colours, CJK text, emoji, resizing, a new tab, and exit closing its tab (10-11). Before a fix in that run it crashed at its first window.

hand.detail: The author used the app by hand on the VM on 10-11, as the committed run record states; the same checks were also driven by tools. Under Wayland a virtual keyboard garbles shifted keys exactly as in Ghostty built at the reference commit on that VM.

lanes.detail: One native run, not a recurring lane. Workspace tests: 6,665 passed, 23 failed on the first run; every failure was fixed or explained and its test binary re-run green. GTK runtime tests: 163 passed, 0 failed. Live GTK window tests: 15 of 18; the 3 DMA-BUF tests need a GPU driver the VM lacks. No sanitizers (Rust supports them on FreeBSD only for x86_64) and no amd64 run.

rows.sub: wasm32 · terminal core, font demo and event loop
rows.claim: The terminal core and the font demo compile to WebAssembly and run in a browser, in Node and under wasmtime, where the event loop's WASI backend passes its tests; three example pages give the same output as Ghostty's. There is no web terminal app, and Ghostty has none either.

builds.detail: The freestanding WebAssembly build is part of the default check script (restored 10-07 after a regression). The event loop also builds for WASI, where its tests run (10-10).

runs.detail: Three example pages ran in headless Chrome against Ghostty's own WebAssembly build: 139 outputs, all identical (10-10). The event loop's WASI backend ran under wasmtime (10-10). Earlier: headless SwiftShader and live Chrome on ANGLE Metal with byte-identical output (07-30); a logging site in Node (09-10).

hand.detail: The author ran all five example pages by hand in Chrome on 10-10, at 3a59e7edc (the author's own statement; no run record is committed). Earlier: one live Chrome run (07-30). The automated example-page checks run in headless Chrome.

lanes.detail: The event loop's WASI backend runs its tests under wasmtime in the default check script: 34 passed, 2 ignored (WASI has no threads), 0 failed, with a check that every loop test ran and a negative control. A browser lane compares three example pages with Ghostty's and checks their constant tables against the module, each with negative controls; it found a bug in Ghostty's SGR example page, fixed in Rustty.

rows.sub: librustty-vt, the terminal library for C
rows.claim: It works on all three desktop OSes and in WebAssembly, with example programs checked against goldens.

builds.detail: Builds on all three desktop OSes (MSVC release on Windows) and for wasm32.

runs.detail: 29 C examples on macOS and 25 on Linux build and run; on Windows one example's output is byte-identical.

hand.detail: A library: exercised by its example programs.

lanes.detail: 586 to 604 library tests per host, Miri on the C API crate, C consumer and header layout checks.
